title: Recommender Systems
tagline: How Netflix, YouTube, and TikTok pick what you see: collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, two-tower retrieval, ranking, and evaluation.
prereqs: Machine Learning. Deep Learning helps for the later steps.

steps.title: The math behind recommenders
steps.why: The core idea of predicting ratings from similar users and items.

steps.title: Content-based vs collaborative filtering
steps.why: Two basic strategies and when each one works.

steps.title: Collaborative filtering in practice
steps.why: User-based and item-based neighbors, with their weak spots.

steps.title: Matrix factorization
steps.why: Learn hidden taste factors from a sparse ratings table.

steps.title: Build a recommender in Python
steps.why: Turn the ideas into working code on a movie dataset.

steps.title: Neural collaborative filtering
steps.why: Replace the dot product with a neural network in PyTorch.

steps.title: Two-tower retrieval
steps.why: How big systems narrow millions of items to a few hundred.

steps.title: Fast nearest-neighbor search
steps.why: Serve embeddings at scale with approximate search indexes.

steps.title: YouTube's deep recommender paper
steps.why: Walk through the classic two-stage candidate and ranking design.

steps.title: Design a recommendation engine
steps.why: See retrieval, ranking, and serving fit into one system.

steps.title: Ranking metrics: MRR, MAP, NDCG
steps.why: Measure whether the right items land near the top.

steps.title: Explore versus exploit with bandits
steps.why: Handle new items and users while still learning from clicks.

projects: Train matrix factorization on MovieLens and report NDCG@10 against a popularity baseline.
Build a two-tower model on MovieLens and serve its embeddings through a FAISS index.
Write a short comparison of three recommenders on one dataset, with metrics and failure cases.
